To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the three types of private sewage system installations are located on sites with different physiographic constraints, that each type is located in a distinct landscape region, that the three types are associated with different land use patterns and that, in the case of alternative systems, these land use patterns are not compact and high-density as predicted in the EIS.
the three types of private sewage system facilitate residential development in rural areas of southeastern Wisconsin, but the development pattern is similar for all three types of system.

(1) alternative sewage systems and holding tanks are not associated with higher density development patterns in Ozaukee County; (2) alternative systems facilitate development on sites with severe physiographic constraints, whereas holding tanks facilitate development on sites that are even more severely constrained; (3) alternative systems are installed in areas of the County that are more densely settled than areas where holding tanks are installed; and (4) holding tanks are installed on sites where conventional systems would be prohibited by local regulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the landscape context of rural residential wastewater systems and how this context is related to the process and pattern associated with rural residential development.
the landscape context of private sewage systems and how these systems influence the process and pattern by which rural landscapes change.
the landscape context of private sewage system development in southeastern Wisconsin, USA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
private sewage systems are not a major factor in the process and pattern change of landscape in the Ozaukee County.
the landscape context of rural residential wastewater systems is complex.

the installation of private on-site sewage systems facilitates residential development in a variety of landscape contexts, but the pattern of development is not strongly influenced by wastewater treatment technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the landscape context of residential development facilitated by private sewage systems in Ozaukee County is characterized by scattered residential patches dispersed within the agricultural landscape.

the three types of private sewage system installations facilitated residential development in a manner consistent with the EIS scenario, but that the development was more dispersed and less compact than anticipated.

private sewage systems, and especially alternative systems, facilitate residential development in rural areas throughout the United States and that the development patterns associated with these systems are not consistent with the compact, higher density patterns suggested by the 1979 EIS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of alternative sewage treatment systems in rural landscapes can facilitate the development of small residential patches that are dispersed throughout agricultural landscapes.
, in this case, the technology was not a significant driver of landscape change.

, in the absence of public policy constraints, private sewage systems facilitate the process of landscape change and that the nature of that change is dependent on the type of sewage technology installed.
